disease_label_per_paper: Rashless varicella-zoster virus encephalitis diagnosed by CSF metagenomic next-generation sequencing (paper Case 1 of two), later complicated by possible VZV vasculopathy
case_selection_note: The paper reports two patients; only Case 1 (68-year-old man) is structured here.
presentation_summary: 68-year-old man with no notable medical history admitted with 3 days of low-grade fever (transiently improved), then sudden limb convulsions and impaired consciousness for 13 h.

Exam: confused, pupils equal and reactive but sluggish light reflex, limbs move slightly to pain, no bilateral pathological signs, neck stiffness (chin-to-chest three finger-breadths); cardiopulmonary and abdominal exam unremarkable. No rash.

MRI: multifocal non-enhancing FLAIR hyperintensities in right temporal lobe, cerebellar vermis, bilateral superior cerebellar hemispheres, cerebral peduncle, and right periventricular region. EEG: mild nonspecific background abnormalities without epileptiform discharges.
LP: opening pressure 200 mmH2O; CSF WBC 400/uL, protein 2.05 g/L, glucose 3.9 mmol/L, chloride 108 mmol/L.
time_zero_definition: Hospital admission (initial MRI, EEG and lumbar puncture); fever onset about 3 days earlier, seizures/impaired consciousness 13 h earlier.

confirmatory_findings.finding: CSF mNGS detected 252 VZV sequences (initial LP sample)
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Subsequent CSF mNGS detected 252 sequences of VZV. CSF mNGS was performed using the initial lumbar puncture sample.
Serum varicella-zoster virus immunoglobulin G (VZV IgG) was positive.

confirmatory_findings.finding: CSF cytology: inflammatory reaction with mitotic figures and suspected atypical lymphocytes
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: CSF cytology was abnormal. Mitotic figures were observed, together with suspected atypical lymphocytes, small lymphocytes, or activated monocytes.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Differential work-up: serum GABAB receptor antibody weakly positive; other serum and CSF autoimmune encephalitis antibodies negative; HIV negative; CSF M. tuberculosis NAT and AFB smear negative
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Serum testing showed weak positivity for gamma-aminobutyric acid type B receptor (GABAB receptor) antibody. Antibodies against NMDAR, CASPR2, AMPA1R, AMPA2R, LGI1, and GAD65 were all negative. The autoimmune encephalitis antibody panel in the CSF was also negative. HIV antigen and antibody testing was negative. Nucleic acid testing for the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex was negative.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Later course: day-45 new acute periventricular infarct with renewed CSF pleocytosis (possible VZV vasculopathy)
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: On day 45 after disease onset ... Follow-up brain MRI suggested a new acute cerebral infarction adjacent to the posterior horn of the left lateral ventricle ... repeat CSF analysis showed a white blood cell count of 140 cells/μL and a protein level of 0.93 g/L
Based on the clinical manifestations, neuroimaging findings, and CSF inflammatory changes, rashless VZV encephalitis was diagnosed.

actual_treatment: intravenous acyclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 h for 21 days
repeat acyclovir course with dexamethasone, aspirin and atorvastatin for day-45 infarct

outcome.source_text_value: His condition improved again, and he was discharged. During more than 3 years of follow-up after discharge, there was no recurrence of VZV encephalitis or acute cerebral infarction.

quality_warnings: Paper reports two patients; only Case 1 is used.
No numeric vital signs or blood tests reported at presentation; quantitative data are CSF values and opening pressure.
Absence of rash at onset is taken from the paper's description of both patients as rashless ('no typical rash at disease onset') and is kept as rankable negative evidence.
CSF mNGS, VZV serology, cytology and autoimmune/TB/HIV exclusion tests are non-ranking.
